title.narrative: High Risk - High Impact Investments in Africa - Capital contribution to IFDK

description.narrative:
Impact Fund Denmark (IFDK) is Denmark’s development finance institution, supporting sustainable private sector investments in developing countries. IFDK invests in sustainable growth and high-impact solutions, mobilising capital to tackle global challenges where the need is greatest. The focus is on investments that offer high development impact and scalable business opportunities.
The purpose of this contribution was to enhance IFDK’s investments in lower income African countries. The country focus was complemented with a high-impact focus in order to priorities investments which expected to generate high development outcomes closely related to the SDGs in local economies, but where the expected risk-adjusted return would be lower than what IFDK can normally accept. A total of DKK 350 million have been allocated to HRHI through three grants targeting climate investments as well as investments that contributed to the generation of decent jobs, in particular for women and youth, bottom-of the pyramid, smallholder agriculture, access to affordable and clean energy, and MSME. The blended concessional finance initiative was integrated into IFDK’s governance structure, and was managed according to current policies and strategies.
Development effects of investments projects often take years to materialize, making them difficult to capture within short reporting periods. As a result, the indicator reporting focuses on tangible outputs, such as the number of investments, as proxies, based on the assumption that these will contribute to long-term development impact. To learn more about the development effects, see the case stories on IFDK’s website, in IFDK’s Annual Report, and in the Open Aid section below.

Development objective: Enhanced IFDK's contribution to climate investments, job creation and inclusive green growth in lower income countries in Africa.
Immediate objectives: 1. Blended concessional finance initiative developed and in operation with increased volume of IFU investments in climate projects with high development outcomes in the lower income countries in Africa. 2. Promote and accelerate IFU’s development of procedures for and experience with identifying and managing projects with high development outcomes in lower income countries in Africa.
